context: A driving coach and student discuss safe driving in bad weather
purpose: Teach: 落ちる/避ける/下がる/決まる/梅雨/渋滞/厳しく/地理

lines.speaker: daichi_kansai
lines.jp: 今日は梅雨入りやし、路面ツルツル滑るから、いつもより厳しく速度を管理せなあかんで。
lines.en: It's the start of the rainy season today, so the road's slippery — we have to manage speed more strictly than usual.
lines.style: Kansai dialect, warm but firm coaching tone with rolling rhythm.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい。雨の日って視界も下がるし、ブレーキの効きも落ちる気がして、いつも怖いんですよね。
lines.en: Yes. On rainy days visibility drops and braking feels weaker too — it always scares me.
lines.style: Polite student register, slightly nervous and earnest with rising intonation.

lines.speaker: daichi_kansai
lines.jp: せやろ。せやから渋滞に突っ込むんやのうて、早めに迂回ルート選んで渋滞自体を避けるんが基本やねん。
lines.en: Right. So instead of plowing into traffic jams, picking a detour early and avoiding the jam itself is the basic rule.
lines.style: Instructive Kansai cadence, casual yet authoritative with practical emphasis.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: なるほど。でも僕、この辺の地理にまだ詳しくなくて、迂回先がパッと決まらないんです。
lines.en: I see. But I'm still not familiar with the geography around here, so a detour route doesn't get decided quickly.
lines.style: Apologetic university-student tone, honest admission with soft hesitation.

lines.speaker: daichi_kansai
lines.jp: ほんなら助手席にナビ広げて、主要な坂道と橋だけでも頭に入れとき。気温が下がる日は橋の上が一番危ないからな。
lines.en: Then spread out a map in the passenger seat and at least memorize the main slopes and bridges — bridges are most dangerous on cold days.
lines.style: Practical Kansai mentoring, listing tips in a steady reassuring rhythm.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: わかりました。あと、強風で枝が落ちる映像をニュースで見て、台風の日は本気で怖いなと思いました。
lines.en: Understood. Also, after seeing branches falling in strong winds on the news, I think typhoon days are genuinely terrifying.
lines.style: Reflective student tone, sharing a recent observation with sincere concern.

lines.speaker: daichi_kansai
lines.jp: せやねん。視界悪い時はハザード焚いて、無理に追い越さんと、安全第一でいこか。ルートが決まるまで焦らんでええで。
lines.en: Exactly. When visibility is bad, put your hazards on, don't force overtakes, and let's go safety-first. No need to rush until the route is decided.
lines.style: Concluding Kansai pep-talk, warm and confident with a closing nod.
